base_override.reason: The engine's per-share figures divide CONSOLIDATED owner's earnings (100% of the operating company, including the noncontrolling interest's share) by the filer's tagged diluted share count, which for this Up-C filer is Class A only (ttm.json: TTM OE $1,488,000,000 on 187,553,000 current-YTD Class A diluted shares = $7.9338/share). Class A is only ~54% of the economic units: Class B shares / OpCo units held by Diamondback and other noncontrolling holders share the same per-unit distributions and are exchangeable 1-for-1 into Class A, so consolidated OE must be divided by total units. A shares_override cannot fix this — overrides fill only absent periods and never replace filed values (the NTNX/VIV precedent). The corrected base pins TTM OE per total unit; it is ~48% below the engine's Class A-basis TTM figure and is the only reason this name does not print a fake high tier off a share-basis artifact. Denominator is the Mar 31, 2026 unit count; Q2 2026 buybacks (~3.0M Class A shares repurchased in the quarter, per the Q2 2026 release) would only raise the figure ~0.8%, so the pin is slightly conservative.
base_override.source: Built from this run's ttm.json TTM owner's-earnings total ($1,488,000,000 = TTM OCF $1,495,000,000 − capex $0 by override − SBC $7,000,000 by override) divided by total economic units of 359,123,000 = Class A 194,312 thousand + Class B 164,811 thousand shares outstanding at March 31, 2026 (Form 10-Q for Q1 2026, Consolidated Statements of Changes in Stockholders' Equity, balance at March 31, 2026). Cross-check against the company's own per-unit math: Q2 2026 consolidated OCF of $487M (statements.json) / 359,123,000 units = $1.356 per unit, vs the $1.37 per Class A share of cash available for distribution the company itself reported for Q2 2026 (GlobeNewswire release, 2026-08-03) — the two agree once Q2 buybacks are allowed for. $1,488,000,000 / 359,123,000 = $4.143427182330288 per unit.

capex_override.ack_reason: Out of band by construction: the band is computed against the last FILED capex value and Viper has never filed one under any candidate tag (last_filed_value is null), so every value flags out-of-band, including the filing-proven $0. This is not an estimate lacking an anchor — it is a figure established by the filer's own cash-flow statements (see source), and no filed capex value exists in any period to anchor to.
capex_override.reason: DATA_GAP:capex — capex missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every candidate tag the engine reads, because Viper is a mineral/royalty owner that buys no property or equipment: operators bear all drilling and completion capex on its acreage. Its investing outflows are acquisitions of mineral interests — growth investment, not maintenance capex (the same distinction the sweep applied to Royal Gold's stream/royalty acquisitions). The filing's cash-flow statement fully accounts for investing activities for all three years with no PPE purchase line, so PPE capex is $0 as a filing fact, not an estimate. Measured impact is nil: the engine's history already carried capex as assumed-zero, so the override changes no OE figure — it converts a silent zero-fill into a sourced, registered decision.
capex_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-25, accession 0002074176-26-000010), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows (p. 50): the investing-activities section for 2025/2024/2023 lists ONLY 'Acquisitions of oil and natural gas interests' $(1,549)M / $(696)M / $(830)M, 'Acquisitions of oil and natural gas interests—related party' $(875)M / $— / $(75)M and 'Proceeds from sale of oil and natural gas interests' $— / $88M / $(3)M, netting to $(2,424)M / $(608)M / $(908)M. There is no purchases-of-property-plant-and-equipment, fixed-asset or capital-expenditure line anywhere in the statement for any of the three years (the balance sheet carries only $8M of other property, equipment and land at FY2025).

moat_against: No pricing power: royalty revenue is a price-taker claim on oil, gas and NGL prices (FY2025 ceiling-test impairment of $768M when prices fell)
Reserves deplete: maintaining per-unit production requires continuous acreage acquisition at market prices (FY2025 acquisitions of oil and gas interests $1,549M + $875M related-party)
Volumes depend on third-party operators' (mainly Diamondback's) drilling and completion pace
Single-basin concentration: essentially all value in the Permian Basin; long-run hydrocarbon demand decline caps the terminal story
Up-C structure: a large noncontrolling interest (OpCo units / Class B) shares consolidated economics ahead of Class A holders, and net debt was $2,173M at FY2025 (being paid toward a ~$1.5B target)
moat_for: Perpetual mineral/royalty interests (96,003 net royalty acres at FY2025) that bear no well capex or lease operating expense — a structural cost advantage no producer can match
Scale: largest pure-play mineral company after the Aug 2025 Sitio acquisition (~$4.0B all-equity); proved reserves 406,035 MBOE, ~78% proved developed producing
Diamondback symbiosis: parent-operator develops Viper acreage preferentially; ~1,388 gross horizontal wells in active development on its Permian acreage at YE2025 plus ~1,370 line-of-sight wells
Cash ROIC history well above cost of capital before the FY2025 non-cash impairment (fundamentals.json roic_proxy 19.9% FY2023, 16.3% FY2024); operating margin 86.5% / 66.4% in FY2023/FY2024
Royalty breakeven far below current commodity prices — cash generation survives troughs that force producers to cut rigs
moat_justification: The largest pure-play mineral and royalty owner in the Permian: perpetual royalty interests that bear no drilling, completion or operating capex, a symbiotic Diamondback relationship supplying a disproportionate share of development on its acreage, and scale that gives it the lowest cost of capital in a fragmented minerals market — a moderate-strong asset moat (6). It is not wider: Viper is a pure commodity price-taker, its reserves deplete and must be replenished by buying acreage at market prices, volumes depend on third-party operators' drilling pace, and essentially all value sits in one basin facing long-run hydrocarbon decline.
name: Viper Energy, Inc.
one_liner: Largest Permian mineral/royalty owner, moat 6/10, zero-capex royalty cash flow — on the corrected per-unit TTM base it barely clears 15%: weighted IRR 15.02% (Tier B), weighted IV@15% $45.11 vs the $45.02 price, but the bear case is Tier D (9.98% IRR), so size it like the conservative end of B.

sbc_override.ack_reason: Out of band by construction: the band is computed against the last FILED SBC value under the tags the engine reads, and Viper has never filed one in companyfacts (last_filed_value is null), so any override flags out-of-band. The value is not an estimate — it is the exact FY2025 equity-based compensation printed in the filer's own 10-K statement of changes in stockholders' equity (see source).
sbc_override.reason: DATA_GAP:sbc — SBC missing for FY2023, FY2024, FY2025 under every tag the engine reads (ShareBasedCompensation / AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense have no facts in this filer's companyfacts). The filer's own equity statement reports equity-based compensation of $7M (FY2025) / $3M (FY2024) / $1M (FY2023). The engine applies this single FY2025 value to every missing period, which overstates FY2023 SBC by $6M and FY2024 by $4M against the same statement's true values — both in the conservative direction of lowering owner's earnings, and immaterial either way (FY2025 SBC is 0.7% of FY2025 OCF of $1,053M). ttm.py prorates the same value across its legs, leaving TTM SBC at the FY2025 figure.
sbc_override.source: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-25, accession 0002074176-26-000010), Consolidated Statements of Changes in Stockholders' Equity (pp. 51-52), row 'Equity-based compensation' credited to additional paid-in capital: $7M for FY2025, with $3M for FY2024 and $1M for FY2023 in the same statement. The cash-flow statement (p. 50) carries no separate equity-compensation addback line — it is inside the 'Other' operating adjustment of $13M / $6M / $3M — which is why EDGAR companyfacts has no ShareBasedCompensation fact for this filer.
